data.title: Caught Out By Ambarella's Slide? Here's What Bears Saw
data.description:
Ambarella has been back in the headlines after reporting record Q1 2027 automotive AI revenue and securing a decade-long, US$800m-plus partnership with Hanwha, the kind of news that often dominates watchlists. For Ambarella shareholders, the loss over the past year was 34.4%, including dividends. If you had bought in a year ago on the earlier edge AI optimism and analyst enthusiasm, how should you now think about the reliance on IoT and concentrated customers?

This theme extends beyond Ambarella. See which of 41 AI small caps may still merit a closer look.

The Two Futures Ambarella Investors Had In Mind

The shares cost US$83.09 at the start of the period, and investors in Ambarella were effectively choosing between two very different stories about where edge AI and IoT might take the business.

On the upbeat side, one narrative saw a fair value of US$90.05, a price implied by assumptions of 14.8% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 14.1%, helped by design wins across edge devices and a unified software platform.

A more cautious view pointed to a fair value of US$57.94, based on 12.1% assumed revenue growth and concerns that reliance on volatile IoT demand and a concentrated Asian fulfillment partner could leave margins exposed to downturns and trade shocks.

What The Ambarella Evidence Actually Tested

The key event was Ambarella’s decade-long, US$800m-plus Hanwha agreement, which supported the bullish view that IoT and edge AI customers could add more predictable orders. Reported results pointed the other way on profitability. The firm still reported a loss in Q2 2027, so the margin recovery that optimistic forecasts relied on remained unproven. Overall, the evidence was mixed.

The lesson is clear. When a thesis hinges on turning design wins into stable earnings, it is important to track the shift in net margin alongside any big contract headlines at other chipmakers.

What Ambarella’s Lower Price Now Asks You To Believe

Ambarella trades at US$54.64, with the shares down 34.4% over the past year. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St sees Fair Value above that level and argues the current quote does not fully factor in its edge and Physical AI focus.

The same Narrative hinges on Ambarella turning automotive, robotics and channel programs into durable edge AI revenue, so any buyer today effectively has to believe those partnerships scale despite memory and supply constraints.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Ambarella turns its growing pipeline of automotive, robotics, and indirect channel partnerships into sustained edge AI revenue while managing supply and memory headwinds for customers."

The price and this Narrative do not agree. → Uncover what this Narrative says Ambarella is actually worth

Ambarella And The Infrastructure Question

Ambarella pulls you toward cameras, cars and edge devices. The obvious story stops there.

Your second step could be further back in the plumbing. All that data from chips and software still has to move, connect and stay secure.

Another business focuses on that digital infrastructure layer. It supplies networking, connectivity and software that keep data flowing between machines and users.

As demand for computing and bandwidth changes, that role can matter more. The interesting part is how such an infrastructure specialist turns that necessity into long-running cash generation.

data.title: Did Strong Sales Growth Just Shift Texas Instruments (TXN) Investment Narrative?
data.description:
• Texas Instruments reported 27.7% fiscal Q3 2026 sales growth, supported by broad demand across industrial, data center and other markets, alongside new AI-enabled CCStudio developer tools and industrial connectivity products announced earlier in November.
  • The CCStudio agentic AI framework and new multiprotocol industrial modules highlight how Texas Instruments is pursuing productivity gains for engineers, which can reinforce long-lived chip design wins in factory automation, IoT and radar systems.
  • Attention now turns to how Texas Instruments' long-life analog franchise intersects with its new AI-enabled CCStudio tools to shape the investment narrative.

Texas Instruments Investment Narrative Recap

To stay in Texas Instruments, you need to believe, as OLetourneau, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, argues, that its manufacturing scale, long product lifecycles and direct sales network keep its analog and embedded parts locked into equipment for decades. The short term swing factor is whether the current 27.7% Q3 2026 sales jump proves cyclical or supports steadier orders as customers absorb higher pricing and capacity investments.

The biggest near term risk is that recent revenue strength reflects a sharp analog upcycle while the stock trades on a rich P/E. Any cooling in bookings or margin pressure could therefore have a negative impact. Management’s capacity build and AI centric tools should help operational execution, but the latest product launches do not materially change that cyclical risk.

The CCStudio agentic AI announcement is the clearest link to Texas Instruments’ latest quarter because it speaks directly to how embedded developers adopt its microcontrollers, wireless parts and radar SoCs. By injecting TI specific data into AI workflows, the toolkit aims to turn long, manual coding and migration projects into faster, more automated work inside tools engineers already use.

For catalysts, that matters if it shortens time to design win and makes it less painful for customers to switch from competing devices into TI silicon. The flip side is execution risk. The framework spans multiple agents, models and device families, so any reliability issues or slower adoption could limit the operational benefit at a time when expectations around AI ready industrial connectivity are rising.

OLetourneau’s narrative arrives at a fair value of $284.32 for Texas Instruments by applying 14.2% annual revenue growth and a future 30.0% profit margin in a discounted cash flow style framework that relies on TI’s long product lifecycles and perceived pricing resilience.

data.description:

Is Oversea-Chinese Banking Still Cheap on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit Oversea-Chinese Banking can earn above the return required by its shareholders. For this bank, the framework leans heavily on its equity base and how productively that capital is used rather than on headline earnings alone.

Book Value is SGD13.73 per share, with a Stable Book Value projection of SGD15.20 per share, so the model assumes the equity layer continues to build over time. Stable EPS of SGD1.99 per share and an Average Return on Equity of 13.11% compare with a Cost of Equity of SGD1.03 per share. That gap yields an Excess Return of SGD0.96 per share, which signals value being created above the required charge for capital.

The dividend lens points in the same direction. The model uses DPS of SGD1.05, a payout ratio of 55.64% and DDM growth capped at 2.63%, which keeps the long term dividend path relatively conservative while still projecting ongoing distributions. Taken together, the Excess Returns work suggests the estimated intrinsic value sits meaningfully above the current share price of SGD27.42. data.title: Here's Why We're Watching AuMEGA Metals' (ASX:AAM) Cash Burn Situation
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. Nonetheless, only a fool would ignore the risk that a loss making company burns through its cash too quickly.

So should AuMEGA Metals (ASX:AAM) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? In this article, we define cash burn as its annual (negative) free cash flow, which is the amount of money a company spends each year to fund its growth. The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Does AuMEGA Metals Have A Long Cash Runway?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. In September 2026, AuMEGA Metals had CA$23m in cash, and was debt-free. Importantly, its cash burn was CA$12m over the trailing twelve months. So it had a cash runway of about 2.0 years from September 2026. While that cash runway isn't too concerning, sensible holders would be peering into the distance, and considering what happens if the company runs out of cash. Depicted below, you can see how its cash holdings have changed over time.

Check out our latest analysis for AuMEGA Metals

How Is AuMEGA Metals' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

AuMEGA Metals didn't record any revenue over the last year, indicating that it's an early stage company still developing its business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. As it happens, the company's cash burn reduced by 4.4% over the last year, which suggests that management are maintaining a fairly steady rate of business development, albeit with a slight decrease in spending. Admittedly, we're a bit cautious of AuMEGA Metals due to its lack of significant operating revenues. So we'd generally prefer stocks from this list of stocks that have analysts forecasting growth.

Can AuMEGA Metals Raise More Cash Easily?

Even though it has reduced its cash burn recently, shareholders should still consider how easy it would be for AuMEGA Metals to raise more cash in the future. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

AuMEGA Metals has a market capitalisation of CA$35m and burnt through CA$12m last year, which is 33% of the company's market value. That's not insignificant, and if the company had to sell enough shares to fund another year's growth at the current share price, you'd likely witness fairly costly dilution.

How Risky Is AuMEGA Metals' Cash Burn Situation?

On this analysis of AuMEGA Metals' cash burn, we think its cash runway was reassuring, while its cash burn relative to its market cap has us a bit worried. We don't think its cash burn is particularly problematic, but after considering the range of factors in this article, we do think shareholders should be monitoring how it changes over time. Taking a deeper dive, we've spotted 4 warning signs for AuMEGA Metals you should be aware of, and 3 of them can't be ignored.

data.title: News Flash: Analysts Just Made A Substantial Upgrade To Their enCore Energy Corp. (CVE:EU) Forecasts
data.description:

The loss per share is anticipated to greatly reduce in the near future, narrowing 60% to US$0.19. We can see there's definitely been a change in sentiment in this update, with the analysts administering a sizeable upgrade to next year's revenue estimates, while at the same time reducing their loss estimates.

data.title: Caught Out By Blackstone's Slide? Here's What Bears Saw
data.description:
If you followed the headlines about Blackstone’s AI bets, data centers and private credit expansion, the recent share slide still comes as a shock. Holding Blackstone from the start of the year would have meant a 24.1% loss, including dividends. If you had put money to work on 1 January 2026 based on upbeat inflows, margin targets and a richer future P/E, what key risks in those original assumptions went uncounted?

The Two Blackstone Stories Investors Had In Front Of Them

The shares cost US$154 at the start of the period, and Blackstone was being debated through two very different yet reasonable stories about what came next.

In the bullish case, Fair Value sat at US$182, 18% above the start price, built on assumptions of 16.7% annual revenue growth and profit margins climbing to 48.9% on a future P/E of 28.6x over three years.

The more cautious script pointed to a Fair Value of US$145, 6% below the start price. It highlighted risks such as rapid infrastructure and private wealth expansion creating operational inefficiencies, despite assumed 15.9% revenue growth and a 53.1% margin.

What The Blackstone Evidence Put Under The Microscope

Blackstone’s Q3 2026 report showed revenue of US$2,918.2m and net income of US$662.4m, with net margin rising to 22.7% from 21.3%. That helped the optimistic case that assumed better profitability, although the margin level still sat far below the near 50% targets in both scripts, so the evidence cut both ways.

The key assumption that got tested was margin expansion. For any other manager you look at, track whether net margin is actually climbing toward the levels built into the revenue and P/E story.

What Today’s US$116 Blackstone Price Already Bakes In

data.title: Income Investors Should Know That Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) Goes Ex-Dividend Soon
data.description:
Regular readers will know that we love our dividends at Simply Wall St, which is why it's exciting to see Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) is about to trade ex-dividend in the next 4 days. The ex-dividend date is one business day before a company's record date, which is the date on which the company determines which shareholders are entitled to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is important as the process of settlement involves a full business day. So if you miss that date, you would not show up on the company's books on the record date. In other words, investors can purchase Johnson & Johnson's shares before the 24th of November in order to be eligible for the dividend, which will be paid on the 8th of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$1.34 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of US$5.36 per share. Last year's total dividend payments show that Johnson & Johnson has a trailing yield of 2.0% on the current share price of US$272.70. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether Johnson & Johnson's dividend is reliable and sustainable. As a result, readers should always check whether Johnson & Johnson has been able to grow its dividends, or if the dividend might be cut.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Dividends are typically paid from company earnings. If a company pays more in dividends than it earned in profit, then the dividend could be unsustainable. Its dividend payout ratio is 79% of profit, which means the company is paying out a majority of its earnings. The relatively limited profit reinvestment could slow the rate of future earnings growth. We'd be concerned if earnings began to decline. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. Dividends consumed 63% of the company's free cash flow last year, which is within a normal range for most dividend-paying organisations.

It's positive to see that Johnson & Johnson's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

Check out our latest analysis for Johnson & Johnson

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Businesses with strong growth prospects usually make the best dividend payers, because it's easier to grow dividends when earnings per share are improving. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. With that in mind, we're encouraged by the steady growth at Johnson & Johnson, with earnings per share up 3.6% on average over the last five years. A high payout ratio of 79% generally happens when a company can't find better uses for the cash. Combined with slim earnings growth in the past few years, Johnson & Johnson could be signalling that its future growth prospects are thin.

Many investors will assess a company's dividend performance by evaluating how much the dividend payments have changed over time. Johnson & Johnson has delivered an average of 6.0% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past 10 years of dividend payments. We're glad to see dividends rising alongside earnings over a number of years, which may be a sign the company intends to share the growth with shareholders.

To Sum It Up

Is Johnson & Johnson an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? Earnings per share growth has been unremarkable, and while the company is paying out a majority of its earnings and cash flow in the form of dividends, the dividend payments don't appear excessive. In summary, while it has some positive characteristics, we're not inclined to race out and buy Johnson & Johnson today.

However if you're still interested in Johnson & Johnson as a potential investment, you should definitely consider some of the risks involved with Johnson & Johnson. Our analysis shows 2 warning signs for Johnson & Johnson and you should be aware of these before buying any shares.

data.title: What Xiaomi Bears Saw Before The Fall
data.description:
If you had looked at Xiaomi on 1 January 2026 and decided to sit it out, the move might feel easier to justify now. For Xiaomi shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 29.2%, including dividends. That decline came alongside rising memory costs, heavier EV losses, and softer smartphone demand reported later in the period. The real question is which early assumptions about margins, capital intensity, or market maturity were already on record before any of that news arrived.

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Xiaomi is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 33 elite gold producer stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Xiaomi Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost HK$39.3 at the start of the period, and anyone considering Xiaomi then had to choose between two sharply different expectations for where the business might be headed.

The bullish narrative saw a Fair Value of HK$66.01, or 68% above the start price. It leaned on Xiaomi pushing deeper into premium smartphones, appliances, and EVs, with analysts assuming 21.3% revenue growth and a 9.1% profit margin over a 3 year horizon.

The bearish case put Fair Value at HK$35.12, or 11% below the start price. That view focused on smartphone saturation and heavier research spending, with analysts in that camp assuming 16.5% revenue growth and a profit margin drifting to 7.6% over roughly the same period.

What The Results Changed For The Xiaomi Thesis

Xiaomi’s later report showed Q2 2026 revenue at C¥108,921.609m and net income at C¥9,462.405m, both below Q2 2025, with net margin sliding from 10.3% to 8.7%. That outcome leaned toward the cautious case on profitability. News of rising memory costs, EV losses and a profit slump reinforced that pressure, so the period cut both ways for the original narratives.

The lesson is simple. When a story leans on margin expansion, track the reported net margin and segment level cost lines rather than only top line growth or product launches.

What Xiaomi's Drop Leaves You Paying For Today

Xiaomi now trades at HK$28.52, with this Narrative's Fair Value sitting above that level. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St frames that gap around Xiaomi's ability to use its Mobile × AIoT ecosystem and premium hardware to reshape its mix.

A buyer today would be assuming heavy AI, EV and R&D spending ultimately turns into durable monetisation across devices, software and higher margin internet services rather than staying mostly a cost line.

"The main thing that has to go right is that heavy long term spending on AI, embodied intelligence and smart EVs, including the planned R&D ramp, converts into sustained monetisation across devices, services and autos rather than remaining a cost drag."

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the higher figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there

Another Way Into Xiaomi's Theme

Xiaomi keeps pulling you toward devices, ecosystems and how people upgrade. One step away, a different business leans on a similar consumer habit.

Your phone and watch are becoming a personal hub for media, payments and health tracking. That shift depends on buyers accepting premium hardware to access richer subscription services.

One large consumer tech group is pushing that model hard. It uses custom chips, higher end devices and bundled apps to steer users deeper into paid services.

If more spending tilts from hardware to subscriptions over time, that pattern could matter. Especially for any company already sitting inside your pocket and on your wrist.
